newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia govt seen reducing grain harvest estimate.
newsitem.headline: Russia govt seen reducing grain harvest estimate.

text.p: A senior independent Russian grain executive said on Friday that government officials had quietly revised down their net grain harvest forecast to 65-67 million tonnes from 70-72 million.
An Agriculture Ministry spokesman said he had not yet received the latest information on the harvest, which is drawing to a close, and declined to provide figures.

Arkady Zlochevsky, president of the private OGO grain trading company, one of Russia's largest, said the ministry was loth to talk about the lower figures. But he said actual output could be several million tonnes higher than the new forecast.
"They are going on the basis of reported output, and do not included grain that producers are not reporting, which probably totals two or three million tonnes," he said.

Gross grain output, not including maize, on all farms as of October 21, the last day for which data was available, was 73.5 million tonnes, including 68 million tonnes on former collective farms, according to State Statistics Committee figures.
About eight percent of the harvest is lost after cleaning.
